subject: ela
intro: Twelfth graders demonstrate knowledge of eighteenth-, nineteenth-, and early-twentieth-century foundational works of American literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics. They connect works to their literary movements and historical moments.

items.prompt:
Realist writers of the late 1800s depicted ordinary life plainly rather than romantically.

What shared THEME or approach did they share?

steps: Realists shared a focus on everyday life and believable detail.
So a shared approach is the honest depiction of ordinary, everyday experience.
solution.answer: An honest, unromantic depiction of ordinary everyday life.

items.prompt: Why compare two works from the SAME PERIOD on a similar theme?

steps: Comparing them shows how the era's writers shared and varied ideas.
So it reveals how the period's writers treated a common theme differently.
solution.answer: To see how writers of the same era treated a common theme similarly and differently.

steps: A movement is a group of writers sharing styles and ideas in a period.
So it is a shared literary style and set of ideas in a period.
solution.answer: A shared literary style and set of ideas among writers of a period.

items.prompt: A group of writers sharing ideas in a period is a literary ____.
Comparing two same-period works shows shared ____.
